item.title: Dr Anna Xambo at Autumn School 2026
item.description: Poster of the Autumn School 2026. Dr Anna Xambó will be giving a keynote on Saturday 21 November 10:00-11:00 on “Listening, Seeing, Tinkering: Sensing the Forest through Sound Data” at the Autumn School 2026: Listening, imagining, sharing and experiencing sound worldliness: between creative, artistic and educational processes.

item.title: Shuoyang Zheng presents at UCL The Art and Science of Creative AI
item.description: Poster of the UCL The Art and Science of Creative AI. Over 50 speakers from across art, science, technology and the creative industries will come together to debate what AI means for creativity, practice and scientific discovery, and how artistic and creative perspectives can challenge and transform current trajectories of AI.

item.title: C4DM Field Trip to Tate Modern - Tarek Atoui
item.description: Group photo by a kind visitor at Tate. Day/time: 3/11/2026 11am-12.30pm Location: Turbine Hall at Tate Modern Charalampos Saitis (COMMA lab) and I (CSAL lab), who are module facilitators of the module Interactive Digital Multimedia Techniques, decided to organise a field trip to visit Tarek Atoui’s sound installation at Turbine Hall (Tate Modern) with the IDMT students, an invitation that we extended to our respective labs and C4DM.

item.title: MSc student Nikhil Bullock contributes to Freesound and live coding with MIRLCa-web
item.description: A screenshot of the landing page of MIRLCa-web. As part of his thesis for the MSc Sound and Music Computing at Queen Mary University of London, Nikhil Bullock has ported the SuperCollider extension MIRLCa, developed by Anna Xambó, to the browser.

item.title: BSc student Haidar Chawki Kassem contributes to rainforest protection in Peru
item.description: A screenshot showing Radar for Detecting Deforestation (RADD) forest disturbance alerts in the Peruvian Amazon. Haidar Chawki Kassem, a graduated student from BSc FT Computer Science and AI, Queen Mary University of London, decided to undertake a research project based on developing a Google Earth Engine workflow that combines Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery with RADD forest disturbance alerts to classify the disturbance state of recently deforested sites in the Peruvian Amazon under the supervision of Dr Anna Xambó (QMUL) and Rory Hodgson (Rainforest Foundation UK).
